idea-plugin.name: LogPose
idea-plugin.description:
LogPose — inspect and mock your Android app's network, right in the IDE

LogPose turns your app's traffic into a clean, structured timeline inside a tool window — and lets you mock any response straight back to the device. No proxy, no certificates, no adb logcat | grep: a one-line OkHttp interceptor emits each exchange and the plugin reassembles it.

Capture

  • One row per HTTP exchange — request and response together, never interleaved, never cut off by logcat's ~4 KB line limit
  • Firebase Cloud Messaging pushes and token refreshes appear inline in the same timeline, so you can read push → API call → UI as one story
  • Duplicate detection flags repeated calls and likely double-submits

Inspect

  • Collapsible JSON trees plus a real IDE JSON editor (folding, line numbers) in Raw mode
  • One-click filters: URL search, NET/FCM type, Method & Status toggles, hide-noise, duplicates-only
  • Copy as cURL, copy JSON or a response body, find within a body
  • Multi-select rows and copy the call sequence as plain text — ideal for bug reports
  • First-class multipart upload (S3 / GCS) metadata instead of raw bytes

Mock & replay

  • Right-click any captured request → Mock this endpoint and serve a response without touching backend or app code
  • Replace the whole body, or merge your JSON into the real response: override one field, add keys, and let everything else stay backend-generated
  • Edit the response field by field — fold what you don't need, tick exactly what to override, and see the original value beside your change
  • Inject latency, timeouts and connection failures, cap how many times a rule serves, and match paths with * wildcards
  • Rules sync to the device over adb, report live hit counts, and clear themselves when you stop capturing — mocked rows are badged, so the timeline never lies about what the app actually received

Requires the logpose-android interceptor in your debug/staging build (a zero-overhead no-op ships for release). Mocking needs logpose-android 1.2.1+. Works in IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio, light and dark.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Your coding agent can read the running app — LogPose now exposes the live capture over MCP, so Claude Code (or any MCP client) can answer "what did the app actually request, and why did it fail?" from real traffic instead of a pasted log line — and can create a mock to reproduce or unblock a state. Click ⚡ Connect Coding Agent to copy the command. Served on the IDE's built-in web server, localhost only, authenticated with a per-project token.
  • Log anything, not just HTTP — LogPose.event("UserDao.insert") { … } puts your own subsystems on the same timeline: database queries, background jobs, analytics, feature flags, navigation. Events carry their own presentation, so they render with no plugin update. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.3.0; older versions keep working unchanged.
  • New look — a redesigned brand mark (a prompt that points north), native IDE context menus, and a roomier, better-organised mock editor.
  • Field-by-field mock editing — edit a captured response as a tree: fold what you don't need, edit any value in place, and in merge mode tick exactly the fields to override (a changed value shows the original beside it). Add new keys, drop to raw text, or hit Compare with original for a side-by-side diff of what the app will actually receive.
  • Merge (patch) mocks — keep the real backend response and deep-merge your JSON on top: override one field, add keys, leave the rest untouched. Merging now recurses into arrays by index, so you can change a field inside data[0] without replacing the array. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.2.1.
  • Mock & replay — right-click a captured request → "Mock this endpoint…" to serve a response back to the app instead of hitting the network: edit status/body/headers, add latency, or simulate a timeout / connection failure. Rules live in a Mocks strip (toggle, edit, delete, hit counts), persist per project, and mocked rows carry a purple MOCK pill. Requires logpose-android ≥ 1.1.0 on the device.
  • FCM push messages in the timeline — Firebase Cloud Messaging pushes and token refreshes now appear inline alongside HTTP traffic, tagged FCM with a NOTIF/DATA/TOKEN badge. Selecting one shows the notification, metadata, and the data payload as a JSON tree. A new TYPE filter (NET/FCM) narrows the stream. Feed events from your FirebaseMessagingService via the new LogPose.logFcmMessage / logFcmToken library API.
  • Failed requests now show why — instead of an opaque "(failed)", the Response and Overview cards display the captured exception (connection reset, timeout, cleartext-not-permitted, …) so the failure is diagnosable.
  • Duplicate-call detection — repeated identical requests fired in a quick burst are flagged with a DUP ×N tag; overlapping non-idempotent calls (double-submits) are highlighted in red, with a warning in the overview and a "Dupes" filter to isolate them.
  • Raw JSON now colors keys vs. values (matching the tree), shows line numbers, and pre-collapses deeply-nested nodes on large payloads.
  • Response headers are hidden by default behind a "Headers" toggle (request headers stay shown) — no more CSP noise drowning the body.
  • Light-theme support (adapts to the IDE theme)
  • Raw JSON mode is now a real editor with code folding
  • One-click filter bar (method/status toggles, Hide-noise switch)
  • Find in request/response, server trace-id in the overview
  • Multi-select rows and copy the call sequence as a plain-text timeline
  • Helpful empty state
